cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: The Sorrel agent has flown her Assembly's flag from a moored barge. The Compact says nothing about flags. I have brought Aldmere's, in case it says nothing about two.

left.label: No flags on Company water
left.outcome: Both come down. Both parties blame you, which is a kind of balance.

right.label: Fly them both
right.outcome: Two flags over one pound. Hesse takes a plate of it.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Aldmere has raised its grain price again and Sorrel's mills are on short time. My principals ask whether the summit could 'lose' a grain barge for a week. Just one. Just once.

left.label: Nothing gets lost here
left.outcome: "Didn't think so. Had to ask."

right.label: A week's delay for repairs
right.outcome: The grain barge sits. The mills run. Crane files.

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: An Aldmere customs cutter has moored beside my convoy with its gun uncovered. It is within its rights. So am I, if I uncover mine. I would rather you told them to cover up first.

left.label: Tell Crane to cover the gun
left.outcome: Crane is appalled that anyone uncovered anything. It is covered.

right.label: Both stay covered, or both leave
right.outcome: Both leave. The pound is briefly very quiet.

cards.speaker: src_telegram
cards.text: ALDMERE GUILDS TO KEEPER STOP SORREL AGENT VANE TO BE DENIED ACCESS TO TOLL BOOK UNDER COMPACT ARTICLE SIX STOP CONFIRM STOP

left.label: Confirm
left.outcome: Vane learns of it from Fennick before you can tell her.

right.label: Article Six says no such thing
right.outcome: Crane, consulted, agrees with you, painfully.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: Lucan Hesse, Sorrel Courier. My readers want to know: is the summit Aldmere's, Sorrel's, or the Company's? On the record. One word will do, and one word is all I'll print.

left.label: The Company's
left.outcome: COMPANY MAN AT THE SUMMIT. Pell frames it.

right.label: The water's
right.outcome: KEEPER: SUMMIT BELONGS TO 'THE WATER'. It is the most read line he has printed.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: A Sorrel vessel has requested passage for 'sixty agricultural laborers' bound for Aldmere. I have counted them. They march in step. I am not permitted to refuse laborers. I am permitted to ask you.

left.label: Laborers pass
left.outcome: Sixty men in step go down the east flight. Aldmere hears of it in a week.

right.label: Hold them for both inspectors
right.outcome: They wait two days and go back west. Solas looks relieved.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: The Aldmere inspector has proposed a duel over the order of passage. A duel. With pistols. I've accepted, obviously. I need a second. You're neutral. Neutral is what seconds are.

left.label: Second her
left.outcome: Both fire wide, formally. Crane is thrilled to have followed procedure.

right.label: Forbid it on Company water
right.outcome: "Spoilsport." Crane, secretly, is relieved.

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: News from Sorrel. There has been shooting at the coalfield. My people are asking whether they will be sent back. I do not know. I would like to tell them the summit is not sending them anywhere.

left.label: The summit sends nobody
left.outcome: "Thank you. They'll sleep. So will I."

right.label: The Company decides that
right.outcome: "It does. I'd hoped you'd lie a little."

cards.speaker: src_telegram
cards.text: SORREL ASSEMBLY TO KEEPER STOP PROTEST DELAYS TO COAL STOP REQUEST SUMMIT OPERATE THROUGH NIGHT STOP COSTS TO BE MET BY ASSEMBLY STOP

left.label: Night operation, at their cost
left.outcome: Lamps on the gate all night. The Coffers fill. The town does not sleep.

right.label: The gate keeps the bell
right.outcome: Sorrel protests to Ardent. Ardent is used to it.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: I have it from a source that the Aldmere inspector keeps his own water gauge. Private. Six years. Why would a customs man count water, Keeper? Give me a line and I'll give you the front page.

left.label: No line
left.outcome: "Suit yourself. I'll ask him. He'll tell me. He can't help it."

right.label: Ask Crane yourself; I'd like to know
right.outcome: "So you don't know either. That's the story."

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: The Guilds instruct me to record every Sorrel cargo weight to the pound. It adds an hour to each passage. I note that I did not ask for this. I note that I shall obey it.

left.label: Obey it; Compact rights
left.outcome: Sorrel's fleet backs up to Lock 7. Vane sends a bill.

right.label: Weigh one in five
right.outcome: "A sampling approach. Irregular. I shall document my objection and comply."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Aldmere has seized a Sorrel coal fleet at Lock 3 over a 'paperwork discrepancy'. Twelve boats. My principals want the summit closed to Aldmere grain until they're released. You can do that. You have the gate.

left.label: Close the summit to grain
left.outcome: Grain stops. Bread in Sorrel rises. Aldmere releases the fleet in four days. Nobody thanks you.

right.label: The gate is not a weapon
right.outcome: "Everything's a weapon. Some of them are just slow."

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: There is an Aldmere man at the inn asking my sergeants what they are paid, and offering more. He is recruiting. Openly. Under the Compact I cannot touch him. Under the Compact you can move him.

left.label: Move him along
left.outcome: He goes down the east flight with a list of names anyway.

right.label: A man may talk at an inn
right.outcome: Two sergeants leave with him. Solas does not mention it again.

cards.speaker: src_telegram
cards.text: ALDMERE AND SORREL JOINT TO KEEPER STOP COMPACT ANNIVERSARY STOP BOTH INSPECTORS TO DINE AT KEEPER'S TABLE STOP THIS IS NOT A REQUEST STOP

left.label: Host the dinner
left.outcome: Crane and Vane argue for four hours about a fish course. It is the best evening in months.

right.label: Host it at the inn, at their cost
right.outcome: Ilse serves them. They tip differently. She remembers which.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: The Courier's Aldmere edition was seized at Lock 2 as 'seditious'. It was about grain prices. I'd like to print the next one at Halfway and send it both ways. I need a room.

left.label: Print at the Company house
left.outcome: Ink on the Company's floor. The Guilds are livid. Sorrel cheers.

right.label: Print at the inn, if Ilse will
right.outcome: Ilse will, for a fee and a column about the cellar.

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: I am recalled to Aldmere for a month to give evidence on the Compact's operation. I note that in my absence there will be no second seal for arms. I note that I have told nobody else this.

left.label: No arms pass while he is gone
left.outcome: "Duly. I am, I find, grateful."

right.label: The Sorrel seal will have to serve
right.outcome: "I note that. I note it with regret."

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: My principals have bought the inn's debt from Cole. Not to call it in. To have it. Sorrel likes having things at the summit. I'm telling you as a courtesy, and because Ilse won't believe it from me.

left.label: Tell Ilse yourself
left.outcome: Ilse is quiet for a long moment, then charges Vane double forever.

right.label: Not the Keeper's business
right.outcome: "Everything at the gate is. That's the job. Isn't it?"

cards.speaker: solas
cards.text: Aldmere has posted a customs cutter at the east flight to inspect every convoy twice. Once here, once below. My men are tired of being counted. I am asking you to make one count enough.

left.label: One count, at the summit
left.outcome: Crane agrees, reluctantly: the Compact says summit. Below stands down.

right.label: Aldmere's flight, Aldmere's count
right.outcome: "Understood." He does not say it is.

cards.speaker: hesse
cards.text: Off the record: both shores are drafting plans to take the canal if the Company falls. Aldmere by law, Sorrel by purchase. On the record: which would you rather worked for?

left.label: Neither; the Company keeps the gate
left.outcome: KEEPER LOYAL, says the Courier, in a tone.

right.label: Whoever fixes the water
right.outcome: He stops writing. "What's wrong with the water?"

cards.speaker: crane
cards.text: I have discovered that the Compact, read strictly, obliges the Keeper to host a joint shore conference at the summit every seven years. None has ever been held. We are, I calculate, eleven years overdue.

left.label: Hold the conference
left.outcome: Delegates from both shores. Three days. Nothing is decided and everyone is impressed.

right.label: Eleven more years won't hurt
right.outcome: "It might. I shall note the date."
